name: Time Out Market Lisboa
seoTitle: Time Out Market Lisbon: A Quick, Reliable Lunch Stop
tagline: A food hall of 26 Lisbon restaurant counters in the Mercado da Ribeira, handy for a quick lunch between sights

description.short: Time Out Market Lisboa fills half of the Mercado da Ribeira at Cais do Sodré with 26 restaurant counters, 8 bars and communal tables. It is about 2 km (28 minutes) on the flat from the cruise terminal. Entry is free, there are no reservations, and it opens daily at 10:00.
description.full:
For a cruise passenger the Time Out Market solves one problem well: lunch for a group that wants different things, fast, with prices on display and no reservations. It also has a clear downside: at peak lunchtime it is loud, crowded and hard to find a seat.

The market opened in 2014 in half of the Mercado da Ribeira, Lisbon's old central market hall, with counters run by chefs and restaurants selected by Time Out's editors.

Getting there from the ship: it is about 2 km west along the flat riverside, around 28 minutes on foot, and the building is opposite Cais do Sodré station. Most people combine it with the Baixa: walk to Praça do Comércio (14 minutes), then on along the Ribeira das Naus promenade. By metro, take the Blue Line from Santa Apolónia to Baixa-Chiado and change to the Green Line for one stop to Cais do Sodré. A taxi takes about 10 minutes.

Timing matters more than anything. Doors open at 10:00; the hall is comfortable until about 12:00, and full from roughly 12:30 to 14:30. If you can eat an early lunch at 11:30 or a late one after 14:30, you will find a table without hovering. At busy times, send one person to hold seats while the others order: each counter gives you a pager and you collect your own food.

What to eat: Portuguese dishes are the point here, so look for grilled fish, octopus, bifana or prego sandwiches, and a pastel de nata for dessert. Each counter posts its menu and prices; expect restaurant prices rather than market prices.

What to skip: the international counters (burgers, pizza, sushi) are not why you came to Lisbon. The older fresh-produce market in the other half of the building is worth a look in the morning, when stalls are open.

From Cais do Sodré you can also take the train to Belém or the ferry to Cacilhas, which makes the market a natural lunch stop on a longer port day.
description.history: The Mercado da Ribeira has been Lisbon's riverside food market since the late 19th century; the current building dates from the early 20th century. As wholesale trade moved out of the city centre, the hall lost much of its business. In 2014 Time Out Portugal took over half of the hall and filled it with counters run by restaurants its critics had already reviewed. The model was copied by Time Out in other cities, but Lisbon was the first. The traditional fresh-produce market still operates in the other half.
description.significance: It is the easiest place in central Lisbon to try several well-regarded kitchens in one sitting, without booking and without language problems. For a group on a fixed schedule, that matters. Cais do Sodré is also a transport hub, with trains to Belém and Cascais and ferries across the river, only a short walk from the Baixa.

directions.general: Located inside Mercado da Ribeira building at Cais do Sodré, between downtown Lisbon and Belém district
directions.fromCruisePort: About 2 km west, 28 minutes on flat ground along the river to Cais do Sodré; the market is opposite the station. Taxi about 8-10 minutes.
directions.publicTransport: Metro: Green Line to Cais do Sodré (direct access). Train: Cais do Sodré station adjacent. Trams: 15E, 25E. Ferries: Cais do Sodré terminal next door. Buses: 706, 711, 713, 714, 728, 732, 760.
directions.parking: Paid parking at Praça Dom Luís I underground car park (short walk). Limited street parking.

seasonal.notes: Individual counters may open later or close earlier than the building.
Late closing as listed in the official FAQ; some parts of the official site simply say 'daily 10:00 to midnight'.

admissionPrices.notes: Free entry. You pay per dish at each counter; prices are displayed and are in line with city-centre restaurants (main dishes typically about €10–20). Cards and cash accepted.

visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: 11:00–12:00 or after 14:30 for a free table. Weekday lunch is easier than weekends.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: No reservations and communal seating: split up, with one person holding seats and the others ordering. Counters hand out pagers. Prices are posted and cards are accepted everywhere. For a quieter meal, come before noon.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: 2–2.5 hours: about 28 minutes' walk each way plus 1–1.5 hours to eat
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Flat 2 km riverside walk from the terminal, or metro/taxi. The hall is on one level with step-free access.
combinableWith: Praça do Comércio and the Baixa (walk back along the river)
Train to Belém from Cais do Sodré
Ferry to Cacilhas from Cais do Sodré
tips: Eat at 11:30 or after 14:30: between roughly 12:30 and 14:30 finding a free table is the hardest part of the visit.
There are no reservations; one person holds seats at the communal tables while the others order.
Most counters give you a pager and you collect your own food, so keep an eye on it while you hold the table.
Prices are posted at every counter; expect restaurant rather than market prices.
Walk there via Praça do Comércio and the Ribeira das Naus promenade: flat all the way from the ship.
By metro: Blue Line from Santa Apolónia to Baixa-Chiado, then one stop on the Green Line to Cais do Sodré.
Look into the traditional market hall on the other side of the building in the morning, when the produce and fish stalls are trading.
Heading to Belém afterwards? Trains leave from Cais do Sodré station, across the road.

highlights: 26 restaurant counters, 8 bars, 6 kiosks and 5 shops under one roof
Free entry; no reservations, communal tables
Opposite Cais do Sodré station: metro, trains to Belém and Cascais, ferries to Cacilhas
About 2 km (28 minutes) on the flat from the cruise terminal
Traditional fresh-produce market in the other half of the building
Cards and cash accepted; 3 ATMs inside
facilities: Communal seating in the central hall
Time Out Academy cooking school and Time Out Studio event space

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Fully accessible with flat floors, wide aisles, and accessible restrooms. Communal tables may be challenging but doable. Some outdoor seating available.
